title: RepoMap repository_map.json

schema_version.description: Document format version. 1.3.0 is the frozen RepoMap v1 contract for Translate. 1.3.0 adds entry points: __main__ blocks, public functions and classes, __all__, and __init__.py re-exports. 1.2.0 adds language-neutral types inferred from annotations, literals, assignments, constructors, and self. 1.1.0 added a signature and a structured body on every function detail. 1.0.0 was the first versioned repository_map.json and did not include those fields.

source.description: Where the map was scanned from. Omitted when the caller does not supply it.

files.description: One record per parsed Python file.

legacyMap.description: Unversioned repository_map.json: a JSON array of file records. Readers still accept this form. New exports use versionedMap.

source.description: Scan input. local is a directory analyzed in place. git is a remote that was cloned, including GitHub URLs.

path.description: Absolute path of the directory that was scanned.

url.description: Git remote URL passed to the clone, unchanged.

stableId.description: Stable id. Prefix is file, class, method, or function. The rest is the repository-relative path plus the definition name, and a line number when the grammar requires one.

file.description: Path of this Python file relative to the repository root.

id.description: File id: file:{path}. Never includes a line number.

imports.description: Module strings imported by this file, in source order, including imports nested in functions. Relative imports keep their leading dots. Duplicates are removed.

import_details.description: Import statements at module scope, including imports inside if, try, for, while, with, and match. Imports inside functions are stored on the function instead.

classes.description: Classes defined at module scope, including classes inside conditional blocks. Classes defined inside functions are listed on that function's local_definitions. Overload stubs are not classes.

functions.description: Functions defined at module scope, including functions inside conditional blocks. Nested functions are listed on the enclosing function. @overload stubs are omitted.

bindings.description: Simple module-level name assignments used to follow aliases, builtins, and values. Includes assignments inside conditional blocks and every name in a chain such as ib = attr = attrib. Unpacking is not a binding.

function_details.description: Body-level detail for every scanned function and method, including functions and methods nested inside other functions. Each detail includes a signature and a structured body for later translation.

dependencies.description: Other files in this repository imported by this file, sorted by relative path. The file itself is not included. External and standard-library modules are omitted.

types.description: Module-level names whose types were annotated or inferred. Function and class statements are omitted; those types live on the function detail and the class.

entry_points.description: Definitions in this file that outside code or a script can start from, plus any __main__ blocks in this file. A re-exported name is recorded on the file that defines it, with reason reexport. reasons is a subset of main, all, reexport, and public. main means a __main__ block calls it or this entry is that block. all means a static __all__ lists the name. reexport means a package __init__.py, or another module's __all__, exposes a definition from a different file. public means the name does not start with an underscore and the defining module has no static __all__ that omits it. Private helpers, nested functions, methods, test modules, and modules under a private path are omitted unless main, all, or reexport names them. A private path has a file or directory name that starts with an underscore, other than __init__.py and __main__.py. Test modules are conftest.py, test_*.py, *_test.py, and files under test, tests, or testing.

type.description: import for `import x`. from for `from x import y`.

module.description: Module named by the statement. Null for a bare relative import such as `from . import name`.

level.description: Number of leading dots on a relative import. 0 for an absolute import.

alias.description: as-name for an `import module as alias` statement. Null for `from` imports; those aliases live on names.

names.description: Names bound by a from-import. Empty for a plain import.

name.description: Imported name, or * for a star import.

alias.description: as-name, or null when the imported name is bound as itself.

bases.description: Base classes that have a dotted name. Bases that are calls or other expressions are omitted.

methods.description: Methods defined directly on the class. Nested functions inside methods are not methods. @overload stubs are omitted.

fields.description: Class and instance attributes. An annotation on the class body is kept. self.attribute assignments in methods are merged in. ClassVar stays on the class. A later annotation is not widened by a conflicting assignment.

id.description: class:{path}:{name}. When the file defines more than one top-level class with this name, the id ends with :{line}.

method:{path}:{class}:{name}. When the class defines this method name more than once, or another method in the file would have the same id, the id ends with :{line}. Methods of a class nested inside a function always end with :{line}.
function:{path}:{name}. When the file defines more than one top-level function with this name, the id ends with :{line}.

kind.description: builtin when the value is a Python builtin name. alias when the value is another name. value for any other assigned expression.

source.description: Builtin or alias name being bound. Null when kind is value.

entryPoint.description: A callable definition outside code can start from, or a __main__ block.

entryReason.description: Why this definition is an entry point. main: a __main__ block calls it. all: a static __all__ lists its name. reexport: a package __init__.py or another module's __all__ exposes it from a different file. public: module-level function or class whose name does not start with an underscore, on a module that is not a test module or a private path, and that is not omitted by a static __all__.

kind.description: function and class are module-level definitions. method appears when a __main__ block, __all__, or a re-export resolves to a method.

name.description: Definition name. An alias such as encode = _encode records the function that alias resolves to.

id.description: Id of this function, method, or class.

reasons.description: Why this definition is on the product surface. Order is main, all, reexport, public.

mainEntry.description: An if __name__ == "__main__" block, or the module body of a __main__.py script. The comparison may be wrapped in and. Calls nested in a function defined inside the block are recorded on that function, not here.

line.description: 1-based line of the if statement. For a __main__.py module body, the line of the first module-level call, or the first statement when the body has no call.

id.description: A __main__ block is not a definition and has no stable id.

calls.description: Calls in the block, sorted, resolved the same way as function calls. Calls inside a nested function or class are omitted.

signature.description: Parameters in source order, type parameters, and the return annotation. Defaults and annotations are expressions. async is true for async def. kind is positional_only, positional, vararg, keyword_only, or kwarg. A bare * is implied when a keyword_only parameter is present and vararg is absent. A / is implied when a positional_only parameter is followed by another parameter.

body.description: Statements in source order. if, for, while, try, with, and match keep their nested statements. return, raise, assignments, and expression statements carry structured expressions, including literals. Nested function and class definitions are markers; the nested function's signature and body, and nested methods, are separate function details. @overload stubs are omitted. elif is an if statement in orelse. An import a, b statement is one entry per alias, matching import_details, with the statement line added.

calls.description: Unique call expressions in this function body, sorted, each written as a dotted name plus (). Calls inside nested functions or classes are not included; those bodies have their own details.

local_imports.description: Imports that appear in this function body and not in a nested function or class.

local_definitions.description: Functions and classes defined inside this function. Definitions nested another level down are recorded on the inner function.

class_name.description: Class that defines this method. Null for a plain function.

types.description: Parameter, local, attribute, and return types. Annotations win. Otherwise the type is inferred from literals, assignments, constructors, or self.

id.description: Same id as the matching function, method, or local definition.

parent_id.description: Id of the function that immediately encloses this definition. Null for module-level functions and for methods defined directly on a class.

resolved_calls.description: One entry per calls item, in the same sorted order, with targets and a classification.

localDefinition.description: A function or class defined inside another function. Its id always includes the line number.

fields.description: Attributes of this nested class, same rules as a module-level class.

name.description: Call expression, identical to the matching item in calls.

targets.description: In-repository definitions this call resolves to. Empty unless classification is resolved or ambiguous. Every target id refers to a definition in this map.

ambiguous.description: True when targets contains more than one definition.

id.description: Id of the targeted function, method, or class.

callClassification.description:
Why a call does or does not point at an in-repository definition.

resolved: exactly one in-repository function, method, or class. targets has that definition.

ambiguous: more than one in-repository definition matches, for example two conditional functions with the same name. targets lists each candidate.

python_builtin: the callee is a Python builtin, either called directly (len) or reached through a binding to a builtin.

external: the callee is imported from a module outside the repository, including the standard library and third-party packages, or re-exported from one of those modules.

dynamic_or_instance: the callee is an attribute of a value or instance (user.save, mapping.get) rather than a statically known definition. Also used for an unresolved dotted call that is not an import of an external or internal module.

unresolved_internal: the name is bound, through an import, to a module or symbol inside the repository, but no concrete function, method, or class definition was found.

unclassified: none of the rules above applied. Typically a bare name with no matching definition, builtin, or import.

nullableExpression.description: An expression, or null when this position is empty in the source.

nullablePattern.description: A match pattern, or null for a wildcard with no nested pattern.

signature.description: The def or async def header, without decorators. Parameters follow source order. positional_only parameters come before the implicit /. keyword_only parameters come after * or a vararg.

type_params.description: PEP 695 type parameters on the function. Empty when the function has none.

returns.description: Return annotation. Null when the function has none.

kind.description: positional_only is before /. positional accepts positional or keyword arguments. vararg is *args. keyword_only is after * or *args. kwarg is **kwargs.

default.description: Default expression. Null when the parameter has no default. vararg and kwarg are always null.

bound.description: Bound expression after the colon. Null when the type variable has no bound.

source.description: Unparsed source of the type parameter, or null when it cannot be rendered.

expression.description: A structured expression. Literals use type constant. A dict key of null is a ** unpacking. Calls keep arguments, unlike the calls list, which only stores the callee name.

statement.description: One statement in a function body. Block statements contain nested statement lists. A function or class statement does not contain the nested body.

pattern.description: A match pattern. class here is a class pattern, not a class statement.

exprConstant.description: A literal. kind null, bool, int, float, and str store value as JSON. Non-finite floats use the strings nan, inf, and -inf. bytes is lowercase hex. complex stores real and imag the same way as a float value. ellipsis has no value. A negative number written as -1 is a unary expression whose operand is the positive literal, matching Python's AST.

exprDict.description: keys and values are parallel. A null key is ** unpacking of the matching value.

exprJoinedStr.description: An f-string. values are string constants and formatted expressions.

conversion.description: Conversion flag. Null when the expression has none.

format.description: Format spec. Null when the expression has none.

exprTemplateStr.description: A t-string. values are string constants and interpolations.

async.description: True for an async for clause inside a comprehension.

stmtIf.description: An if statement. elif is another if in orelse.

exception.description: Exception type. Null for a bare except.

name.description: Name bound by as. Null when the handler has no as clause.

exc.description: Raised exception. Null for a bare raise.

cause.description: Expression after from. Null when the raise has no from clause.

targets.description: Assignment targets from left to right. a = b = 1 has two targets.

value.description: Assigned value. Null for an annotation without a value.

stmtExpr.description: An expression statement. A docstring is a string constant here.

stmtImport.description: An import or from import inside the function. Fields match importDetail, plus the statement line. import a, b is split into one object per alias.

optional_vars.description: Target of as. Null when the item has no as clause.

stmtFunction.description: A nested function marker. The function's signature and body are a separate function detail with the same name and line.

stmtClass.description: A nested class marker. Methods are separate function details. bases lists dotted names; other base expressions are omitted.

patternAs.description: A capture or wildcard. pattern and name are both null for _.

inferredType.description: A language-neutral type. Java and C++ translation reads this instead of the annotation expression. primitive covers int, float, bool, str, bytes, and complex. set is also used for frozenset. none is JSON null's type. unknown means inference stopped. never means the function does not return. optional is T | None. union has two or more members and does not include none. class is a named type; role instance is a value of that type and role type is the type object itself. id is set when the class is defined in this repository.

typeSource.description: How the type was learned. null when the shape is known but not from an annotation, literal, assignment, constructor, or self. *args without an annotation is a tuple for that reason.

repeated.description: True when every element has the same type, as in tuple[int, ...] or *args.

role.description: instance is a value of the class. type is the class object, including cls on a classmethod.

parameters.description: Parameter types in source order. Null for Callable[..., R].
Parameters in signature order. An annotation is kept. Otherwise a default literal or constructor is used. The receiver of a method is source self.

locals.description: Names assigned in the function, in first-binding order. Parameters are not repeated here.

attributes.description: self or cls attributes this function assigns, in first-binding order.

returns.description: Return annotation when present. Otherwise the common type of the returned expressions. A function with no return has type none. A raise with no return has type never. Yield makes the return unknown unless it is annotated.

scope.description: instance for self.attribute and for an annotation that is not ClassVar. class for a class-body assignment or ClassVar.
